From the point of view of Steve - when CCP refuse to licence it alone for totally understandable "Defending a lawsuit is expensive, regardless of the outcome" reasons - this sort of stuff is trivia. If Wizards/Hasbro were to agree to patent and Deckmaster, this sort of stuff - can I reprint Anson? can I use the "Animalism" symbol? can I use the tri-snake symbol on cardbacks? - is really just nickle and dime contractual addenda. (Assuming you needed Wizards' consent, and that WW/CCP didn't already own those things.)

In the context of a go-it-alone "Well, hmm, do we actually need Hasbro's consent?" - which wasn't the situation Steve Wieck was contemplating, obviously - it all becomes a little more murky. Can I reprint Temptation of Greater Power or Arika? Can Hasbro issue smackdowns for using the Quietus symbol? And so on. If either Paradox and/or OneBookshelf are willing to contemplate that in a world without CCP being involved, it might become more relevant.

Messages.Author: brettscho

Well, that's assuming that a video game company would want to make a card game. It will be interesting to watch what they want to do. They could very well leave the RPG stuff in the hands of Onyx Path, and whoever does the LARP stuff, and focus on making video games with the IP. And making a card game is very different from both RPGs and video games! And considering how much competition there already is for card games these days... I'm not sure I'd want to dive in. Nobody but FFG has really made the LCG model sing for them. AEG tried with doomtown, but it doesn't look like they've had anywhere near the success that FFG has had. Messages.Author: GreyB
Messages.Body:
I suspect Paradox has other plans with WoD and will consider everything else merchandise and promotional on their products, but thats not a bad thing. Rebooting VTES however will still require all the other parties owning IP, perhaps this becomes easier for other parties if paradox backs them up politically.

> BenPeal wrote:
> Is there a way to remake V:TES that would make this community happy?
>
I feel the community is hooked to all the intricacies and quirks of VTES and since it's out of print for some time now, many people have invested a lot to get cards, so they could feel pot committed with lack of a better term. If a remake would mean incompatibility with their current collection, I suspect a lot will quit.

I don't believe it's possible to remake a backwards compatible VTES if one of the goals is to circumvent IP. VTES should continue on, with PDF expansions if need be.

However if VTES trudges on with PDF expansions, there still can be an alternative, but should involve people with domain knowledge in VTES who could translate all the intricacies of VTES into a new game format and perhaps make it better. So over time people will move on without causing major trauma to the community (unlike herds, communities are quite fragile due to the unavoidable individualism).

Some suggestions for a new format:
- Ditch predator/prey relation (last man standing wins)
- Rename 'pool' to influence
- Ditch term "bleeding", everything is an attack on influence
- Ditch tapping (circumvent IP)
- An action always costs at least 1 counter, be it influence of life
- All actors (vampires,imbued, etc) have life (or essence?), no distinction (makes mechanics easier)
- Keep disciplines, rename to skills, new symbols (circumvent IP).
- Ditch allies (introduce werewolfs, mages and whatnot as first class citizens)
- Less in-depth focus on vampire world, vamps vs mages vs werewolfs vs mummies etc.
- Keep politics system, change stuff around to avoid IP
- Introduce new and cool means of destroying influence
- Introduce an influence ceiling as another means of winning (get 60 influence or kill the rest to win the game).

So the new format encompasses whole of WoD, not just vampires, should have a faster pace and can live side by side with the out of print VTES. And VTES players can maintain hope VTES will see a reboot.

Heck, start a thread "Let's make a new WoD game" and let the community join in

-1 Strength

> vice versa.
>
It was - in part - the fact that this licence wasn't renewed that led to V:TES dying. CCP appeared to have been looking to get rid of a lot of their White Wolf physical products, but as I recall some initial work had been done on "the next set" so it didn't look like CCP were going to kill it at the point of the renewal.

It's entirely possible that some of the intellectual property in V:TES was transferred to White Wolf, but it's also possible that some of it was being used under licence, or some other arrangement. For example:

- the intellectual property involved in the card text of any card created by the Wizards of the Coast design teams

- the intellectual property involved in the rules and rulebook. There are long-standing issues in gaming law about the copyrightability of individual mechanics, and that sort of thing. But whole works - such as an entire rulebook - are protected by copyright law. White Wolf (LSJ) clearly updated it, edited it etc., but they may have done so under licence. This also gets into the whole area of derivative works.

- card art. This is one of those areas where things could get extra weird, because the original artist may have retained some rights, or may have licensed it to Wizards (or, for that matter, White Wolf/CCP) for a certain period of time or for particular uses etc. Card art can be changed, of course, and has been on a variety of library cards - but would you want to reprint older vampires with different art?

- logos (not the name, the logo). Does Hasbro have any intellectual property rights over the V:TES logo? Was that transferred to White Wolf? Was it used under licence?

- symbols. Who designed the symbols for things like "political action", or "Quietus"? Who owns any intellectual property rights for them?
